Business Manager, Distribution Job at AXA Mansard




        
    

        
        AXA Mansard is one of the foremost Financial Institutions in Nigeria, that has been offering world class financial services over the years.

We are recruiting to fill the position below:

 Job Position: Business Manager, Distribution

Job Location: Lagos

Job Objective / Purpose of Job


	Upskill and motivate Advisors towards effectively implementing sales strategies for retail insurance sales.


Responsibilities
     

            
    




	Supervise Advisors and sales of insurance products.
	Role play with key prospects through the sales process; understand customer needs and propose approaches for handling objections and closing business.
	Monitor Advisors liaison with customers.
	Actively seek new business opportunities and client accounts, do presentations to defend and convert business by doing a portfolio review of all accounts.
	Compile and send in monthly variable pay for all Advisors within the SBU to Sales & Marketing Support Team by the second working day of every month.
	Present to MUIC businesses that are N10m and above with a Loss Ratio of ≥ 40% and Combined Ratio of ≥80%.
	Review Advisors’ sales reports to establish trends and identify areas for improvement.
	Build and promote strong, long-lasting customer relationships by partnering with them and understanding their needs.
	Identify emerging markets and market shifts while being fully aware of new products and competition status.
	Identify appropriate product mix for Advisors and viable sales strategies to be implemented.
	Manage and maintain weekly, monthly and all required sales reports.
	Own recruiting, objectives setting, coaching and performance monitoring of Advisors.
	Identify trends in Retail business and proactively advise ASM/Group Head on potential actions to take.
	Identify and escalate actual and/or potential operational and administrative issues to the ASM/Group Head.
	Assist in identifying required resources and personnel to achieve the revenue budget of the Group.
	Presentation of the SBU performance at the Monthly Divisional MPR, QBR & Budget meetings.
	Carry out continuous check on spokes monthly.
	Seek approval for accepting/processing transactions when required.
	Ensure that Advisors capture complete and accurate information on the CRM database/Workbench.


Requirements
Education/ Professional Qualification:


	Bachelor’s Degree in any field from a reputable tertiary institution.
	Professional qualifications (i.e. CII, CIIN or other of similar equivalence) will be an advantage.


Experience:


	Minimum 4 years of experience in Financial Services of which 2 years’ should be in the Insurance Business (Underwriting, Sales or Operations).

Assistant Logistics Manager Job at APM Terminals




        
    

        
        APM Terminals is the global terminal operating arm of the A.P. Moller-Maersk Group. APM Terminals operates a Global Terminal Network of 76 operating port and terminal facilities and 117 Inland Services operations in 59 countries around the globe.

We are recruiting to fill the position below:

 Job Position: Assistant Logistics Manager

Ref. ID: R197003
Job Location: Lagos

Key Responsibilities
     

            
    




	You will support the Logistics Manager in planning, coordinating, and executing import and logistics operations, with a focus on regulatory compliance, cost efficiency, and timely shipment delivery.
	Manage end-to-end import logistics operations, ensuring timely shipment clearance and delivery while maintaining agreed lead times.
	Maintain accurate import documentation and compliance with requirements including Form M, PAAR, and SONCAP.
	Resolve operational issues such as clearance bottlenecks, manifest errors, shipment discrepancies, and documentation gaps.
	Coordinate activities across Asset Maintenance, Warehouse, Finance, suppliers, freight forwarders, customs agents, and regulatory bodies.
	Identify operational inefficiencies and implement improvements that strengthen turnaround time, accuracy, cost efficiency, and reliability.
	Maintain reliable freight portal data, communicate structured updates, escalate risks, and recommend solutions that minimize business impact.
	Monitor changes in import laws and regulations and ensure compliance with relevant international, national, and local requirements, including Maersk guidelines on third-party management.
	Success in this role will be reflected through clearance and delivery lead-time adherence, documentation accuracy, compliance, fewer operational delays, cost optimization, stakeholder satisfaction, and contributions to process improvement.


What We Are Looking For


	Continuous improvement mindset: we are looking for someone who brings a thoughtful improvement mindset—curious about how work gets done and motivated to make meaningful, sustainable improvements over time.
	Hold a Bachelor’s Degree in Logistics, Supply Chain, or a related field.
	Bring at least five years of experience in import or logistics operations.
	Demonstrate strong working knowledge of Nigerian import regulations and systems, including NCS, SON, and NSW.
	Apply sound judgement when managing shipment delays, regulatory requirements, documentation risks, and operational uncertainties.
	Communicate clearly with internal teams and external stakeholders while providing timely updates and practical solutions.
	Take initiative, coordinate cross-functional activities, and resolve complex logistics matters without requiring constant supervision.

From our roots as the pioneer in pay-as-you-go &ldquo;PayGo&rsquo;&rdquo; solar energy for off grid homes, we have grown into one of the most advanced connected asset &nbsp;financing platforms in the world, empowering a broad range of customers to achieve progress in their lives.

We are recruiting to fill the position below:

Job Position: Finance Manager - Nigeria

Job Location: Nigeria

What This Role Actually Is


	This is a hands-on, high-ownership position.
	You will be a finance lead for the Nigeria entity &mdash; responsible for the monthly management reporting pack, executive commentary, the IFRS 9 Expected Credit Loss model, treasury and compliance matters, and the unit economics that inform commercial decisions across the market.
	You&#39;ll manage the end-to-end monthly close: accruals, prepayments, intercompany, depreciation, FX. You&#39;ll produce variance analysis that isolates market-specific effects from one-off items. You&#39;ll monitor the loan book, analyse repayment behaviour by cohort, and own provisioning and bad debt trends. You&#39;ll support statutory and regulatory reporting, manage documentation for funding and compliance processes, and support due diligence as needed.
	And then &mdash; because this is Nigeria &mdash; you&#39;ll also be a commercial partner. You&#39;ll sit alongside the commercial team to interrogate unit economics, model new product launches, assess pricing and supply decisions, and build the financial cases for leadership and board discussions.
	This is not a role where the strategy happens upstairs and the finance team keeps score. You&#39;ll shape both.


What Makes It Different


	Most finance roles at this level have inherited structures, established processes, and reporting cadences that largely run themselves.
	This one asks for more ownership than that. You&#39;ll identify automation opportunities, strengthen controls, and ensure IFRS compliance in areas where judgement genuinely matters: IFRS 9, IFRS 16, IAS 21, revenue recognition, IFRS 18 readiness.
	You&#39;ll also have direct exposure to one of Africa&#39;s largest and most dynamic fintech markets, working alongside local and regional leadership to navigate a fast-changing regulatory and commercial landscape. That&#39;s a professional education you can&#39;t buy.


What You Bring


	Qualified Chartered Accountant (ICAN, ACCA, CA or equivalent), with a demonstrable track record in finance management or a senior finance role, including hands-on ownership of statutory and management reporting cycles.
	Deep, applied IFRS knowledge &mdash; particularly IFRS 9, IFRS 16, IAS 21, and revenue recognition &mdash; and proven ability to manage audit processes end-to-end, from file preparation to auditor queries.
	Exceptional financial modelling and communication skills: you can build a complex multi-scenario model in Excel and present its conclusions clearly to a CFO or a lender in the same week.
	Big 4 training (PwC, Deloitte, EY, KPMG) is a strong advantage. Working knowledge of the Nigerian fintech, lending, or asset-financing sector is a plus, though not required &mdash; curiosity and commercial instincts matter more.&nbsp;


The reality check:


	This role will ask a lot of you. The business is scaling fast, the reporting obligations are real, and the market&#39;s dynamics require precision.
	There will be months where the close feels tight and the audit feels relentless. You&#39;ll be operating across strategic and operational levels simultaneously &mdash; and some days the most important thing on your plate will be debugging a provisioning model, not presenting to leadership.
	If that sounds manageable, it probably is. If it sounds energising &mdash; you&#39;re probably the right person.


What You&#39;ll Find Here:


	A front-row seat in strengthening the financial infrastructure of one of Africa&#39;s largest asset fintech businesses, in one of its most important markets.
	A mission where every asset financed is a tangible improvement in a customer&#39;s daily life.
	And genuine ownership &mdash; the kind where your judgement shapes how this entity reports, controls, and makes decisions, not just maintains them.

title: Job Openings at Kimeric Nigeria Limited
content:
Kimeric Nigeria Limited is a Company that has acquired a reputation for rendering quality Onshore/Offshore supply and engineering services to the Oil and Gas industry in Nigeria and West Africa sub-region.

We are recruiting to fill the following positions below:

1.) Cost Estimating Lead III

Job Location: Akwa Ibom

Job Description
     

            
    




	The Cost Estimating Lead will provide oversight and supervision for cost estimate preparation, quality assurance reviews, project costing, scheduling, and cost-control activities across project milestones.
	The role will also support process improvements and provide leadership and consulting to the Estimating Supervisor.


Key Responsibilities


	Coordinate with the Project Management Team to resolve project-related issues.
	Participate in project meetings and discussions with internal teams and external clients.
	Prepare and review project costing reports for management.
	Provide cost control and planning advice to the PMT.
	Support cost estimate preparation, verification, and quality assurance reviews.
	Contribute to improvements in estimating processes, tools, and quality assurance practices.


Skills & Qualifications


	Previous experience in a closely related position and/or cost & schedule estimating.
	Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering is required.
	Strong project cost planning, scheduling, and reporting skills.
	Strong analytical, consulting, mentoring, and computing skills.
	Excellent negotiation, influencing, interpersonal, and communication skills.
	Ability to adapt to changing priorities.
	Previous experience in the Oil & Gas industry is required.


Method of Application 
Interested and qualified candidates should send their Application to: [email protected] using the Job Position as the subject of the email.

 

2.) Drilling Logistics Lead III
